subject: Isolated network pilot: runbook clarifications and resourcing asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Isolated network pilot: runbook clarifications and resourcing asks

Team —

Following the kickoff with NetBridge yesterday, they want us to validate a minimal runbook for an "islanded" private deployment (VPC + on-prem appliance) before committing to a pilot. I sketched a short draft (attached) and flagged gaps where we need input or formal exceptions. High-level asks: familiar / quick summary below.

Quick asks (please reply inline or mark ownership):
- Network setup: who will own the VPN/SD-WAN and the BGP peering configs? NetBridge expects us to provide an ops checklist they can follow. (owner: ??)
- KMS/HSM access: NetBridge needs confirmation of envelope encryption model + key rotation window. Can Security confirm we can support customer-managed keys for the appliance? (owner: Kimberly)
- Oncall & escalation: proposed oncall rotation during pilot = 24x7 for first 2 weeks, M-F 9–5 afterwards. Can Platform accept this delta or do we ask for dedicated SRE support from the customer? (owner: Grace)
- Audit & retention: NetBridge requires 1y audit logs, exportable to their SIEM. Need clarity on retention costs and the retention policy for KV cache traces. (owner: Soojin)
- Fallback plan: we need a graceful fallback to hosted model if latency/throughput targets fail. Ops needs a clear rollback step. (owner: Jordan)

Attachments: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (scope + timeline), runbook-draft.md (runbook with gaps), network-diagram.png (sketch).

Target decision window: can we capture all decisions by end of day 2028-07-18 so NetBridge can lock procurement?

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin | Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[m] 415-555-0147

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, NetBridge Ops <ops@netbridge.io>
Date: 2028-07-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated network pilot: runbook clarifications and resourcing asks

Thanks Marcus — good summary. A few clarifications from my side:

1) Ownership split: Platform can own the Redwood service-side config (firewall rules, route tables, appliance AMI/containers). NetBridge needs to own the customer network side (SD-WAN, on-prem switch, BGP on their edge). We can provide a "Network Handoff Checklist" but we should not be the single owner of their edge configs.

2) Oncall: we cannot commit Platform SRE to 24x7 for an indefinite stretch without a formal paid support addendum. For the pilot we can do 24x7 for the first 7 days and then 9–5 (M-F) with an escalation path into the SRE rotation during business hours. If NetBridge wants 2-week 24x7, we should propose a paid pilot support package (scope + $). Kimberly, can you weigh in on any compliance implications of a paid 24x7 support?

3) Fallback: agree with Marcus — we need an automated fallback path: if p95 latency > 400ms for > 10 minutes we should route to a compatible hosted model and flag operators. I will file INFRA-1198 to track automated failover steps and test checklist.

I'll own the rollback steps and make a concise ops runbook entry. Marcus — please confirm if NetBridge requires us to manage BGP sessions or only provide route filters.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake | Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, NetBridge Ops <ops@netbridge.io>
Date: 2028-07-16T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated network pilot: runbook clarifications and resourcing asks

Looping in a bit of architecture detail so procurement and NetBridge have realistic asks:

- KV cache & persistence: for islanded mode we recommend a local NVMe-backed cache with TTL+periodic snapshot exported to object storage. We should not export raw KV traces; rather, expose summarized metrics and audit events. Cost estimate in attached draft (runbook-draft.md).
- Audit logs / SIEM: we can stream audit events (JSON) to a customer-managed collector over TLS. Retention to 1y is supported but expect incremental storage cost; ops estimate ~200GB/month for NetBridge pilot footprint.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration in the appliance, but HSM-attested keys require a separate compliance review. Kimberly, if we want to promise HSM attestation in the pilot we will need a scoped SOC/compliance exception and additional testing (2–3 weeks).
- Test plan: propose 3-step validation: connectivity dry-run (1 day), functional load test (2 days), failover test (1 day). We should include acceptance criteria (p50/p95 targets, success rate for cached hits).

I'll update the runbook with these specifics. NetBridge Ops — if you can confirm expected QPS and concurrency that will help make storage + cost estimates accurate.

— Soojin
Sojin Lee | Staff Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, NetBridge Ops <ops@netbridge.io>, Kevin Park <kevin.park@greenbank.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated network pilot: runbook clarifications and resourcing asks

Thanks everyone — summary / decisions for NetBridge and next steps below. I've uploaded a consolidated runbook and action tracker to the Drive link (see metadata).

Decisions captured:
- Network ownership: NetBridge will own customer-edge configs and BGP on their side; Redwood to provide a handed-off "Network Handoff Checklist" and validate routes during dry-run. (owner: NetBridge / Jordan to verify route filters).
- Oncall support: Redwood will provide 24x7 coverage for first 7 days of pilot. NetBridge requested 14 days; we proposed a paid pilot support addendum for days 8–14. Kimberly to prepare compliance note and pricing by 2028-07-20.
- KMS/HSM: We can support customer-managed KMS keys in the appliance. HSM attestation requires an exception and additional testing (2–3 weeks) — Kimberly will confirm feasibility and gating tests.
- Audit retention: We will stream audit events to NetBridge collector; retention to 1y approved, incremental cost estimate provided in runbook (Ops estimate ~200GB/month).
- Failover: Jordan to implement INFRA-1198 checklist for automated failover (threshold: p95 > 400ms for 10m). Trial run scheduled during functional load test.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Jordan: INFRA-1198 runbook entry + rollback steps (due 2028-07-22)
- Soojin: update runbook with KV cache and test plan, attach load test parameters (due 2028-07-20)
- Kimberly: compliance note + HSM exception feasibility + pricing for extended support (due 2028-07-20)
- Marcus: finalize pilot statement of work (SOW) and send to NetBridge procurement (due 2028-07-19)

NetBridge Ops (ops@netbridge.io) — please reply with expected QPS and concurrency by 2028-07-19 so we can finalize sizing.

I'll mark this thread as 'pilot-runbook/ready-for-SOW' in the tracker. If there are any changes to owners/timelines call them out inline.

Best,
Marcus
